subject: Incident taxonomy: remediation SLA targets + ownership sign-off
body:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, Feb 3, 2025 at 9:12 AM PST
Subject: Incident taxonomy: remediation SLA targets + ownership sign-off

Neha / Priya,

Sharing the proposed remediation SLA targets for taxonomy v1 so we can get leadership sign-off this week and unblock ENG-4830 + the incident-bot rollout.

Scope reminder: production incidents for Hosted API + Dedicated pools. Private is included where Redwood is primary day-2 operator. Security incidents remain governed by Security IR, but we’ll share the metadata fields.

Definitions (for consistency with our current incident process):
- TTM = time-to-mitigate (stabilize / stop customer impact)
- TTR = time-to-remediate (permanent fix merged + rolled out / verified)

Proposed targets (v1):

SEV1 (broad customer impact / total or near-total outage)
- Routing/control plane failures (smart-routing, policy, config push): TTM 15m / TTR 3d
- Capacity exhaustion / autoscaling unable to meet demand (Dedicated + Hosted pools): TTM 30m / TTR 5d
- Runtime crash / kernel regression (widespread 5xx or hard failures): TTM 30m / TTR 5d
- Edge/gateway (streaming disconnects, TLS, gateway saturation): TTM 30m / TTR 5d

SEV2 (major degradation, partial outage, elevated 5xx/latency impacting subset)
- Routing/control plane failures: TTM 60m / TTR 10d
- Capacity exhaustion / autoscaling: TTM 90m / TTR 10d
- Runtime crash / kernel regression: TTM 90m / TTR 10d
- Edge/gateway: TTM 90m / TTR 10d

SEV3 (minor degradation, limited scope, low customer impact)
- All categories: TTM same business day / TTR 30d

Customer tier note:
- Enterprise/Dedicated incidents (contracted SLA) require Support + CS comms within 30m for Sev1 and 60m for Sev2, even if we don’t have a full RCA yet.

Ownership expectations (to avoid “paper ownership”):
- SRE: incident process + IC, severity validation, on-call routing, and ensuring category/owner assigned within 15m of declare
- Platform: routing/control plane category owners (primary)
- Infra/Fleet: capacity exhaustion/autoscaling category owners (primary)
- Runtime: runtime crash/kernel regression category owners (primary)

Questions for sign-off:
1) Are you comfortable with the Sev1 routing TTM at 15 minutes? (This is the one we expect to be most visible and the highest “pressure” target.)
2) Are you OK setting the category owner at declare time as “required,” with a reclass window post-incident? We can enforce this via incident-bot, but want to align before we make it mandatory.
3) Confirm resourcing: we’ll need 1 platform eng + 1 SRE for 1–2 weeks to finish bot + dashboards wiring.

Thanks,
Sean

—
Sean Gallagher
SRE Sponsor | Redwood Inference


On Mon, Feb 3, 2025 at 10:06 AM PST, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, Feb 3, 2025 at 10:06 AM PST
Subject: Re: Incident taxonomy: remediation SLA targets + ownership sign-off

Thanks Sean.

From Platform’s side:
- I’m comfortable with the 15m TTM for Sev1 routing/control plane as a target, *if* we explicitly allow “mitigate” to include safe-mode fallbacks (e.g., regional shed + pinned model fallback policies) vs requiring full recovery. The playbook needs to say “mitigate = stop user-visible errors” not “restore ideal behavior.”

- I agree category + owner should be required, but I’d strongly prefer the rule to be: required within 15 minutes of declare (not necessarily in the first modal submit) to avoid slowing down declaration when we’re still triaging. Practically, IC can declare quickly and then fill in the field once we know whether it’s routing vs capacity vs gateway.

Resourcing:
- I can commit Mina (Routing) for 1 week on ownership mapping + bot autosuggest, and Ethan for review/sign-off on the control plane categories. If we need a second full week, I’ll need to shuffle a milestone; flag by end of this week.

One more detail: “capacity exhaustion vs routing overload” boundary is still fuzzy in practice. I’d recommend we bias toward “capacity exhaustion” when the symptom is queue growth / admission control / 429/503 from pools and the routing layer is behaving nominally.

Priya

—
Priya Natarajan
Platform Sponsor | Redwood Inference


On Mon, Feb 3, 2025 at 11:02 AM PST, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, Feb 3, 2025 at 11:02 AM PST
Subject: Re: Incident taxonomy: remediation SLA targets + ownership sign-off

Agree on the “mitigate includes safe-mode fallback” language — we’ll encode that in the policy doc + incident-bot help text.

On the category requirement: we can enforce “must be set within 15m of declare” via the bot (it can open a follow-up modal / nag the IC channel). That seems like the best compromise.

Re resourcing, thanks — Mina + Ethan sounds good. SRE will cover the bot + process changes; we’ll pull Devon for the Slack modal changes and validation.

Neha — once you confirm, we’ll finalize the table and publish as the v1 baseline (and run a 30-day review to tune targets based on actual MTTR).

Sean


On Mon, Feb 3, 2025 at 12:41 PM PST, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, Feb 3, 2025 at 12:41 PM PST
Subject: Re: Incident taxonomy: remediation SLA targets + ownership sign-off

Approved with the clarifications below.

1) Sev1 routing/control plane TTM = 15m is signed off. I agree with Priya: mitigation can be “degraded but stable” (fallback/safe-mode) as long as customer-visible errors stop and we communicate clearly.

2) Category + owner requirement: make it mandatory within 15 minutes of declare (not blocking initial declaration). Reclassification after the fact is fine, but we need a single “official” category in the postmortem + dashboards.

3) Resourcing: confirmed. Use Mina + Ethan from Platform, Devon from SRE/tooling, and keep SRE accountable for rollout + training. If Platform needs a second week beyond what Priya noted, escalate early — don’t silently slip.

Next steps:
- Sean: please update the SLA table to include the mitigation definition and the “within 15 minutes” rule, then post the final link in the ENG-4821 initiative and #announcements once we have a date.
- Priya: make sure the routing/control plane categories have clear examples (what goes where) to avoid argument during incidents.

Thank you both — this should reduce the handoff churn we’ve been seeing.

Neha

—
Neha Kapoor
Engineering Leadership | Redwood Inference
